Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa huwa al-'Aziz al-Hakim﴾: That is, the Almighty, who prevails over His command, the All-Wise in His management and His making.

﴿Lima taqulluna ma la taf'alun﴾: That is, for what reason do you say, "We have done such and such," when you have not done it? The interrogative here is for rebuke and reproach.

﴿Kabura maqtan 'inda Allah﴾: That is, it was great in hatred. Al-maqt (hatred) is the most intense dislike; al-maqit and al-mamqut are the one who is hated.

﴿An taqulu ma la taf'alun﴾: That is, your saying what you do not do is hated by God with the most intense hatred.

﴿Saffan ka-annahum bunyanun marsus﴾: That is, lining up in rows; and "marsus" means fitted tightly together, with no gap in it.

﴿Lima tu'dhunani﴾: That is, when they said that he was "adar" (afflicted with a hernia), a lie, so He rebuked them for their lie and for their harming him.

﴿Wa qad ta'lamuna anni rasul Allah ilaykum﴾: That is, do you harm me while you know that I am the Messenger of God to you?

﴿Falamma zagha azagha Allah qulubahum﴾: That is, when they deviated from the truth by harming Moses, God turned their hearts away, that is, He inclined them away from guidance.

﴿Wa Allahu la yahdi al-qawm al-fasiqin﴾: That is, those who committed wickedness and went to extremes in wickedness, so they became unfit for guidance.

﴿Ya bani Isra'il﴾: That is, the sons of Ya'qub, who was titled Isra'il. He did not say "O my people" as Moses said, because he (Jesus) was not from them, for he was born without a father, and his mother was a truthful woman (siddiqah).

﴿Falamma ja'ahum bil-bayyinat﴾: That is, with clear proofs of the truth of his message, through the dazzling miracles.

﴿Qalu hadha sihrun mubin﴾: That is, they said of the miracles that they were sorcery.

Meaning of the verses:

God the Exalted says, ﴿Sabbaha lillahi ma fi as-samawati wa ma fi al-ard﴾: all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth has glorified Him, by the tongue of speech and the tongue of state, and He is the Almighty, who prevails over His command and cannot be resisted in His will, the All-Wise in His making and His management of His dominion. After He praised Himself with this, He addressed the believers with His words: ﴿Ya ayyuha alladhina amanu lima taqulluna ma la taf'alun﴾. The address is general, but what is meant is a group of believers who said, "If we knew the most beloved of deeds to God the Exalted, we would do it." When they came to know it, they were too weak for it and did not act, so God the Exalted rebuked them in this verse, and it remains a general legislation until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever says "I have done" when he has not done is a liar, and lying is a wretched attribute; and whoever says "I will do" and does not do is one who breaks his promise, and breaking a promise is a wretched attribute. In this way God trains His servants in truthfulness and fulfilment. His words ﴿Kabura maqtan 'inda Allah an taqulu ma la taf'alun﴾ mean: your saying "we will do" and then not doing is something for which its doer is hated with the utmost hatred, that is, it is hated with the most intense dislike.

His words ﴿Inna Allaha yuhibbu alladhina yuqatilsuna fi sabilihi saffan﴾ mean: lined up in rows, pressed together, with no gap between them, as if they were a building firmly fitted, one part upon another, with no defect or gap in it, as though it were sealed with lead.

His words ﴿Wa idh qala Musa li-qawmihi﴾: that is, remember when Moses said to his people from the Children of Israel, "O my people, why do you harm me, when you know that I am the Messenger of God to you," while you know that I am truly and sincerely the Messenger of God to you. They harmed him with every kind of harm, with their venomous tongues and their deviant opinions. Among that was their saying that Moses was "adar," which is why he does not wash with us. "Adar" means having a hernia, which is the swelling of the testicle.

His words ﴿Falamma zagha﴾: that is, they deviated from the truth after knowing it with the utmost knowledge; they preferred falsehood to truth, evil to good, and disbelief to faith. God punished them by turning their hearts away from guidance, as a vengeance from Him upon them. This is because it is His custom regarding one to whom news is presented and who refuses it after knowing it, then is called to it and does not respond, then is encouraged to it and is not drawn to it, and continues in evil by choice. At that point, what he has chosen of wickedness, disbelief, injustice, or criminality becomes for him a nature and a fixed disposition that does not change or alter. On this basis is to be understood similar statements such as: ﴿Wa Allahu la yahdi al-qawm al-fasiqin﴾, ﴿Wa Allahu la yahdi al-qawm al-zalimin﴾, ﴿Wa Allahu la yahdi al-qawm al-mujrimin﴾, and ﴿Wa Allahu la yahdi al-qawm al-kafirin﴾, because He has led them astray according to His custom of leading astray, so no one other than God can guide a servant whom God has led astray knowingly. This is the meaning of His words in Surat an-Nahl: ﴿Fa inna Allaha la yahdi man yudill﴾ [Verse 37].

"Indeed I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what is before me of the Torah." This is proof of the truth of my call, since in what I call to, namely the worship of God alone, I have not opposed what is in the Torah, the Book of God Almighty, which is before you; our agreement is evidence that the source of our legislation is one, namely God Almighty. Just as you believed in Moses, Aaron, David, and Solomon, believe in me, for I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what is before me of the Torah and giving glad tidings of a Messenger who will come after me whose name is Ahmad. Therefore the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I am the answer to the prayer of my father Ibrahim and the glad tidings of Isa." When Ibrahim was building the House with Isma'il, they were saying what God informed of in His words: ﴿Rabbana wab'ath fihim rasulan minhum yatlu 'alayhim ayatika...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 129], the verse.

His words ﴿Falamma ja'ahum﴾: that is, Muhammad ﷺ came to them with clear proofs, that is, the arguments that show the truth of his message and the obligation to follow him in belief and in law. They disbelieved in him and said of the Qur'an, "This is clear sorcery," just as Pharaoh said it about Moses.

And just as the Jews said it about Jesus, peace be upon him.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A demonstration of God's independence from His creation: all that is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God, and what He has legislated for His servants of acts of worship and laws is only for their benefit and the good of their souls, that they may be perfected in spirit and character and be happy in both lives.

2- The prohibition of lying and breaking promises, for the saying of one who says "I will do such-and-such" and does not do it is a lie and a broken promise. Therefore it is among the hatred that is the most intense dislike, and whoever God hates, He has hated him with the most intense hatred, and how can one who is hated by God prosper?

3- The virtue of jihad, unity, and harmony, and the prohibition of disagreement and fighting; and that the ranks are torn apart, whether physically or morally.

4- A warning against persisting in sin after sin, for it leads to being sealed and to the deprivation of guidance.

5- A demonstration of the disbelief of the Jews in Jesus, peace be upon him, and they increased in disbelief by disbelieving in Muhammad ﷺ.

6- A demonstration of the disbelief of the Christians, for they rejected the glad tidings of Jesus, returned them to him, and did not believe in the one he gave glad tidings of, Muhammad ﷺ.

﴿while he is being invited to Islam﴾: That is, while this one who fabricates lies against Allah is being invited to Islam, which is submission and surrender to the judgment and law of Allah.

﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾: That is, whoever wrongs and then continues to wrong, such that wrongdoing becomes his nature, will no longer be receptive to guidance, so He deprives him of it according to Allah's established way in this matter.

﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾: That is, the polytheists, with their lies against Allah and their distortion of the Islamic call and their fighting its people, want to extinguish the light of Allah, the Qur'an and what it contains of light and guidance, with their mouths. This is impossible, for extinguishing the light of the sun or the moon is easier than extinguishing a light that Allah does not want extinguished.

﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance﴾: That is, He sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) with guidance, meaning human guidance.

﴿and the religion of truth﴾: That is, Islam, since it is the true religion established by sincere revelation.

﴿to make it prevail over all religion﴾: That is, to give it victory over all other religions, until only Islam remains as a religion.

﴿although the polytheists dislike it﴾: That is, although the polytheistic disbelievers dislike its victory and its prevalence over the religions.

Meaning of the verses

Allah says: ﴿And who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾, while he is being invited to Islam, the true religion. There is no one more wrongful than this person, ever. His wrong is incomparable to this, which is the meaning of His words in the first verse [7]: ﴿And who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾. That is, he fabricates lies against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says things about Him that He did not say, and legislates things He did not legislate, as was the case with the polytheists of Quraysh, who attributed to Him a son and a partner, forbade the sawa'ib, the bahira and the ham, and said regarding the worship of their idols, "If Allah had willed, we would not have worshipped them," and other such lies and fabrications against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And His words "while he is being invited to Islam" refer to the fact that if this had been in the days of ignorance, when there was no messenger and no Qur'an, the matter would have been lighter. But to lie against Allah while the light is clear, the revelation is descending, and the Messenger is calling and explaining, is a greater matter and a greater wrong.

His words in the second verse [8]: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾: That is, those liars against Allah, who say of the Messenger, "He is a sorcerer," and of the Qur'an, "It is manifest sorcery," want to extinguish the light of Allah, which is the Qur'an and what it contains of correct beliefs and laws of guidance. With what do they want to extinguish it? With their mouths. Can the light of Allah be extinguished by mouths, like the light of a candle or a lamp? Indeed, when Allah wills to complete His light, extinguishing the light of the moon or the sun is easier than extinguishing it. Let them know this, and let them desist from their failing attempts, for Allah wants to complete His light, even if the polytheists dislike it. **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 61, Verses 10–14**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"Shall I direct you to a trade?"*: That is, shall I guide you to a profitable trade.

*"That will save you from a painful punishment."*: That is, the profit in it is your deliverance from a painful punishment that awaits you.

*"You believe in Allah and His Messenger."*: That is, you affirm Allah as Lord and God, and Muhammad as the prophet and messenger of Allah, exalted is He.

*"And strive in the cause of Allah."*: That is, you expend your wealth and your lives in jihad (striving) in the cause of Allah, exalted is He.

*"That is better for you, if you only knew."*: That is, entering into this profitable commercial transaction is better for you than abandoning it out of greed for your own survival and the survival of your wealth, even though nothing endures in this abode.

*"He will forgive you your sins and admit you to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden."*: That is, this is the pure profit in exchange for that perishing, transient price, which is wealth and self, although everything belongs to Allah, exalted is He, who is the One who grants you yourselves and your wealth.

*"That is the great triumph."*: That is, deliverance from the painful Fire, then entry into Paradise and attainment of its enduring bliss, is truly the great triumph.

*"And [there is] another [favour] you love: help from Allah and an imminent victory."*: That is, and an additional bonus you certainly love: it is help from Allah to you, and an imminent victory, the conquest of cities and towns, and what follows from that of exaltation, happiness and well-being.

*"And give good tidings to the believers."*: That is, and give good tidings, O our Messenger, to the sincere believers of that triumph and this bonus.

*"Be helpers of Allah."*: That is, that you may support His religion, His Prophet and His allies.

*"As said Jesus, son of Mary."*: That is, so be you, O believers, like the disciples (al-Hawariyyun, the companions of Jesus). The disciples were the first to believe in him, and they were twelve men.

*"The disciples said, 'We are helpers of Allah,' and a faction of the Children of Israel believed."*: That is, in Jesus, peace be upon him, and they said that he was a servant of Allah who was raised to heaven.

*"And a faction disbelieved."*: That is, from the Children of Israel, who said that he was the son of Allah, and that He raised him to Himself.

*"So We supported those who believed against their enemy."*: The two factions fought, so We gave victory to and strengthened those who believed.

*"And they became dominant."*: That is, prevailing and superior.

**Meaning of the verses:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I direct you to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ That is: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, shall we direct you to a trade of great profit, whose fruit is deliverance from a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter? And His words ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives﴾ are the capital you advance: faith in Allah and His Messenger in its true sense, and jihad in the cause of Allah with self and wealth. I draw your attention to the fact that this commercial transaction is better for you than not entering it, if you know its profit and benefit.

﴿He will forgive you your sins and admit you to Gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: this is deliverance from the worldly and otherworldly punishment first, then the forgiveness of your sins and your admission into Gardens beneath which rivers flow, that is, beneath their palaces and trees, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden, that is, a lasting abode.

Second, then the Truth increased their encouragement, saying: ﴿That is the great triumph﴾, which is deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise. There is no triumph greater than this ever. Moreover, there is for you, in addition to this great profit, what He, exalted is He, informed of with His words: ﴿And [there is] another [favour] you love﴾, that is, another benefit you love: help from Allah, that is, for you against your enemies and for your religion over all other religions, and an imminent victory for Mecca and the rest of the cities and villages in the Arabian Peninsula and beyond. His words, exalted is He, ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾ mean: give good tidings, O our Messenger, to those who believed in Us, in Our Messenger, and in Our promise and warning, of the occurrence of what We have mentioned in full. It has been fully realized for them, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿O you who have believed﴾ are a second address in this noble context. He addressed them by the title of faith as well, since faith is the driving, motivating force. He said: ﴿O you who have believed, be helpers of Allah﴾, that is, commit yourselves to supporting your Lord and true God in His religion, His Prophet and His believing allies. Say as the disciples said when Jesus, their prophet, called them to support him, saying: "Who are my helpers in the cause of Allah?" (that is, who will support me while I am turning to Allah? Support His religion and His allies). They answered him, saying: "We are helpers of Allah." So be you, O Muslims, like them, and they, may Allah be pleased with them, were as he asked of them.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿So a faction of the Children of Israel believed, and a faction disbelieved; then We supported those who believed﴾: that is, they fought, and We supported and strengthened those who believed, namely those who said that Jesus is the servant and messenger of Allah whom his Lord raised to heaven, against their enemy, namely the disbelieving faction who said that Jesus is the son of Allah whom He raised to Himself. Allah is exalted above having a son.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿so they became dominant﴾: that is, prevailing and superior, until the Jews schemed to corrupt the religion that Jesus brought, which is Islam, meaning the worship of Allah alone in the manner He prescribed. At that point none remained among the supporters except a few scattered helpers here and there. Disbelief and trinitarianism prevailed, and this state continued until Allah sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). Then whoever among the Christians joined Islam joined it, and by Islam they became dominant over their enemy, the polytheists who deified Jesus and were bewildered about his nature: at one time they said he is God, at another that he is the son of God, and at another that he is the third of three, God. Those who lead them astray and keep them in these labyrinths are the self-interested leaders and the ignorant blind followers among the subordinates, just as their counterparts within Islam did when they turned it into sects and factions. Yet Allah has pledged to preserve Islam until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever seeks it finds it pure, as it was revealed in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ). Whoever does not seek it, and seeks misguidance, finds it in every age and every land.
